newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils await developments in Asia/U.S..
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils await developments in Asia/U.S..

text.p: European vegetable oil traders will take their cue from developments in Asian and U.S. markets in the coming week.
Palm oil prices could steady in the coming week with signs of a build up in Malaysian exports supporting the market.
"Recent export numbers seem good but a lot of people still believe that palm oil is fundamentally weak despite this," said one trader.
Recent data from Malaysian cargo surveyor Caleb Brett put local palm oil exports during July at 722,389 tonnes against its previous estimate of 634,753 tonnes.
However, most players want to see these figures confirmed by the PORLA in its monthly report.
"If exports are rising stocks should stay below one million tonnes, but most people want to see the figures confirmed by PORLA before they change their ideas on the market," said another trader.
Traders said they would be looking at the local disappearance rate closely when the PORLA figures are released.
Soft oils remain stuck in a weather rut which is keeping business at a low level.
"Most people stay clear of the market while Chicago is having its yearly weather-based gyrations," said a trader.
The recent bullish trend in the U.S. dollar has limited the downside of the market when Chicago takes a dive while buyers' reluctance to follow the upside has on the whole restricted any increase.
"Last week one major player started to pay higher prices and seems to have succeeded in pushing prices up further than most people would like to see them go," said another trader.
Coconut oil prices look set to drop further with good supplies at origin as the peak of the copra harvest approaches.
In Rotterdam the cif price of coconut oil has fallen $15 to $20 a tonne in the last week. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
